name: Syria
summary_text: Syria is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. Articles 520/517 of the Penal Code criminalise “sexual acts against nature” and public indecency; there is no legal gender recognition. Since the fall of the Assad regime (December 2024), the situation has worsened: the Guardians of Equality Movement documented “waves of violence” against Syrian transgender women in the first two months of 2025, implicating both non-state armed groups and security forces in multiple cities, and February 2025 videos showed authorities arresting trans women. Digital targeting (entrapment via apps, extortion) is documented across the conflict period. For a visitor: active conflict, trans-targeted violence waves, no recourse whatsoever.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: The Guardians of the Gem report on LGBTQIA individuals in Syria after the fall of the Assad regime (April 2025) returned no extractable text at fetch time (image-based PDF).

sources.title: 2.8.2. Treatment by state, non-state and societal actors | European Union Agency for Asylum
sources.claim_summary: EUAA Syria Country Focus, section 2.8.2: treatment of LGBTIQ persons by state, non-state and societal actors.

sources.title: Syria | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): Articles 520 and 517 criminalise 'sexual acts against nature' and public indecency; no legal gender recognition and no prohibition of nonconsensual intersex interventions; during the 2011-2024 conflict, violence on SOGI grounds escalated - Islamist groups executed and publicly tortured sexual and gender minorities (particularly queer men and trans women); government forces arrested people on morality charges, committed enforced disappearances and sexual violence in detention.

sources.title: Audacity in Adversity: LGBT Activism in the Middle East and North Africa | HRW
sources.claim_summary: HRW report (April 2018) 'Audacity in Adversity': LGBT activism in the Middle East and North Africa - includes Syria's Article 520 criminalisation and the situation of LGBT Syrians amid the conflict.

sources.title: At home and abroad, LGBT Syrians fight to have their voices heard - Syria Direct
sources.claim_summary: Syria Direct (Oct 2020): 'At home and abroad, LGBT Syrians fight to have their voices heard' - Amira al-Tabbaa's activism since 2004 helping those kicked out of work or home; in 'gay-friendly' Damascus cafes friends spoke 'only in whispers'; 'We need to break the door of the closet that they put us into and get out: We deserve life.'

sources.title: Gay Refugees Addresses U.N. Security Council in Historic Meeting on LGBT Rights - Newsweek
sources.claim_summary: Newsweek (2015): two gay refugees from Syria and Iraq testified at the first-ever UN Security Council meeting on LGBT rights (closed session, co-sponsored by the US and Chile) about constant fear of violence and death under authoritarian governments, militant groups and ISIS.

sources.title: Syrian authorities crack down on gay men | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (June 2010): Syrian authorities raided private gay parties, arresting over 25 men - charged with 'homosexual acts', drugs, or 'obscene' parties; families refused to pay bail; police monitor cruising areas; Gay Middle East called for repeal of the 'antiquated' Article 520 of the 1949 Penal Code.
